correctness.rationale: Read all-parameter proof. A complement of a subset dominates rook graph iff it meets every row or every column; thus dominance complex is A∪B where A is join of p copies of ∂Δ^{q−1} (sphere dimension pq−p−1) and B join of q copies of ∂Δ^{p−1} (sphere pq−q−1). Intersection K has combinatorial Alexander dual nerve ∂Δ^{p−1}*∂Δ^{q−1}, a sphere of dimension p+q−3, hence integral homology of S^{pq−p−q}. For p,q≥3 its complete one-skeleton and coned-off missing row/column triangles imply simple connectivity; integral Whitehead/Hurewicz identify K≃S^d with d≥3. For p=2 or q=2, K is a sphere with two disjoint open opposite facets removed, deforming to S^{q−2} / S^{p−2}; p=q=2 gives S^0. Since K→A,B land in higher-dimensional spheres they are null (connectedness handles d=0), so homotopy pushout yields A∨B∨ΣK. Independent exact face and mod-2 chain calculations for 2×2,2×3,2×4,3×3,3×4 verified predicted Betti degrees. Infinite theorem rests on cover and homotopy argument, not finite checks.

originality.rationale: The exact row/column domination predicate is present in Mertens (2024) but his primary paper counts dominating sets and gives a generating polynomial rather than the homotopy types of all complement-dominating subsets. Matsushita–Wakatsuki develop dominance complex duality and compute other examples but the inspected theorems do not supply this all-parameter three-sphere wedge. Published rook neighborhood and cut complexes use different functors.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent rook dominance-complex classification or a stronger abstract graph-product theorem may predate the exact wedge, despite inspected primary literature.
The theorem is nonequivariant, not a claim of PL/simple-homotopy splitting; finite mod2 checks alone are not integral proof.

value.rationale: Complete integral homotopy classification, including low-dimensional boundary parameters and repetitions, of a fundamental two-parameter graph family; topology does not follow mechanically from the already known domination polynomial and provides reusable structure for dominance complexes.
